one_line: Co-Presence is a shared sticky-note canvas where humans and outside agents edit together.
what_it_does: Live peer-synchronized canvas with structured WebMCP tools for reading, arranging, annotating, and proposing changes while enforcing refusals.
leverage_rationale: Shared live state, awareness, structured reads, and refusal-aware mutations make agent collaboration materially more reliable than UI driving.
leverage_evidence: About text describes eleven WebMCP tools, direct tab sync, shared board state, and refusal as a return value.
Frames show a persistent multi-board canvas, but text and action sequence are too small to verify.
execution_rationale: The concept and UI are coherent, but there is no actual video and the packet does not demonstrate a completed end-to-end workflow.
execution_evidence: Devpost screenshot shows a polished two-pane sticky-note canvas.
Frame sheets show repeated canvas states and one auxiliary panel, without legible end-state proof.
impact_rationale: Clear value for teams or individuals who want agents working visibly beside them on a shared board, though the target workflow is broad.
impact_evidence: Pitch identifies simultaneous human/outside-agent editing and shared state as the problem.
creativity_rationale: The shared-room framing and agent refusal/negotiation behavior are a fresh interaction model for WebMCP.
creativity_evidence: Outside agents collaborate on the same canvas rather than operating through a separate chat.
Agent actions receive visible embodied motion and can be refused.
usability_note: Canvas is legible as a concept but dense and evidence of actual operation is limited.
red_flags: No video transcript or live end-to-end evidence.
standouts: Human and multiple outside agents share one live spatial surface.
advance_reason: Distinct collaboration model and strong WebMCP delta; execution needs observation.

one_line: Threadline keeps research claims and provenance inspectable until a human makes them canonical.
what_it_does: Evidence graph for contested claims with staged sources, typed relations, bounded verdicts, and human review of agent proposals.
leverage_rationale: Structured canonical state, provenance, deterministic inspection, and proposal/rejection feedback are substantially more reliable than an agent clicking a graph UI.
leverage_evidence: Eight in-page tools expose sources, claims, typed relations, groups, and bounded verdicts.
Rejected proposals and reasons are returned through get_workspace for later revision.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent, unusually complete research workflow and video-backed product states, though frames are largely deterministic and not all actions are shown.
execution_evidence: Video is 115 seconds and screenshot visibly shows unresolved state, 8/8 tools ready, pending proposals, and human authority boundary.
Frame sheets show reset and inspect-evidence states with nine sources and structured claim review.
impact_rationale: Researchers and readers of contested online claims have a real need for provenance and separation of evidence from inference.
impact_evidence: Product directly addresses repeated-source distortion and autonomous summaries becoming “facts.”
Visible review queue flags duplicated claims and unverified magnitude.
creativity_rationale: The argument-debugger framing, typed epistemic relations, and human-canonical workflow are highly original and deeply pursued.
creativity_evidence: Separates source, support, contradiction, qualification, and amplification.
Non-destructive staged proposals preserve human authority.
usability_note: Information-dense but purpose-built; visible filters and review queue support auditing.
red_flags: Frame sheets emphasize deterministic fixture states rather than broad live behavior.
standouts: Clear canonical-state boundary and provenance-first argument model.
advance_reason: Strong across all four criteria with concrete product and workflow evidence.

one_line: Project Desk is a local-first workspace for human-controlled planning and agent deliverables.
what_it_does: Maintains tasks, decisions, evidence, deliverables, and activity history in one browser-local project workspace.
leverage_rationale: Structured workspace state and explicit decision/completion gates make agent handoffs substantially more dependable than chat plus UI automation.
leverage_evidence: About text describes reusable handoffs, classified evidence, stale-evidence reconciliation, and human completion control.
Frames show a project workflow overview but not agent calls.
execution_rationale: The product scope is coherent and the packet includes seven gallery images, but no video or clear completed deliverable is shown.
execution_evidence: Description specifies tasks, decisions, deliverables, evidence, and history as integrated surfaces.
Frame sheet shows a loaded project with instructional cards, but static overview only.
impact_rationale: Many knowledge-work projects suffer from scattered chat context; durable local workspace and explicit uncertainty have broad practical value.
impact_evidence: Clear audience/problem pairing in the description.
creativity_rationale: The local-first, evidence-classified, human-gated project record is a thoughtful synthesis beyond a generic task manager.
creativity_evidence: Consequential decisions and completion remain human-controlled.
Facts, assumptions, missing information, and activity are first-class.
usability_note: Workflow is understandable, though evidence does not show the full work pass.
red_flags: No video and no visible generated deliverable.
standouts: Strong durable handoff and uncertainty model.
advance_reason: Credible product and impact with meaningful structured-state leverage.

one_line: AgentBridge gives websites control over which agent tools are exposed and what actions require approval.
what_it_does: Control and permission layer for discovering, gating, and confirming WebMCP tools across merchant and agent experiences.
leverage_rationale: Permission-aware tool discovery and human confirmation change agent reliability and governance beyond generic UI automation.
leverage_evidence: About text describes merchant control, agent access permissions, and WebMCP discovery.
Packet claims ChatGPT invocation, but frames are not supplied for review beyond a static gallery capture.
execution_rationale: The pitch is coherent and the submission has a public repo, but evidence is primarily screenshots and requested/aspirational gallery descriptions.
execution_evidence: Facts report public repo and live demo.
About text describes inspector, merchant controls, and confirmation flow; no end-to-end frame evidence is clear.
impact_rationale: Website owners have a real need to constrain agent capabilities and protect consequential commerce actions.
impact_evidence: Merchant control and permission problem is clearly articulated.
creativity_rationale: A governance/control-plane framing for WebMCP is useful and reasonably original, though the individual controls are familiar.
creativity_evidence: Combines tool discovery with permission controls and human confirmation.
usability_note: Control-layer concept is clear; workflow details are not well evidenced.
red_flags: Evidence appears more packaging-oriented than behavioral.
standouts: Makes agent permissions a first-class product surface.
advance_reason: Promising infrastructure concept, but execution evidence is too thin relative to stronger packets.
